Professional biography

João Feres Júnior · Full Professor of Political Science at IESP–UERJ.

João Feres Júnior is a Full Professor of Political Science at the Institute for Social and Political Studies of Rio de Janeiro State University (IESP–UERJ), where he has taught since 2010. His research encompasses political communication, political behavior, democratic theory, race relations and conceptual history.

He coordinates the Institute for Democracy: Institutions, Behavior, Public Sphere and Diversity (INCT ID-ICED), based at IESP–UERJ. The institute studies challenges and threats to democracy in comparative perspective, connecting institutions, political behavior and the public sphere with inclusion and sustainability in Brazil and South America.

He earned a bachelor’s degree in Social Sciences and a master’s degree in Philosophy at the University of Campinas. He subsequently completed a master’s degree and a PhD in Political Science at the Graduate Center of the City University of New York, receiving his doctorate in 2003.

He has taught at Rutgers University, Brooklyn College, IUPERJ and UNIRIO. He served as executive editor of UERJ University Press from 2019 to 2023 and, in 2023, as National Secretary for Analysis, Strategy and Coordination at the Brazilian Presidency’s Secretariat for Communication.

At IESP, he coordinates the Multidisciplinary Study Group on Affirmative Action (GEMAA), the Brazilian Legislative Observatory (OLB) and the Laboratory for Media and Public Sphere Studies (LEMEP). Within LEMEP, he develops initiatives including Manchetômetro, the Public Debate Monitor and Politics in Networks.

In addition to academic books and articles, he contributes to reports, bulletins and discussion papers on media and politics, legislative behavior and racial inequality. This work also involves training researchers and contributing to public debate.

Brief biography

Academic profile

João Feres Júnior is a Full Professor of Political Science at the Institute for Social and Political Studies, Rio de Janeiro State University (IESP–UERJ), where he has taught since 2010. He holds a PhD in Political Science from the Graduate Center of the City University of New York (2003). His research covers political communication, political behavior, democratic theory, affirmative action, race relations, and conceptual history. He coordinates the Institute for Democracy: Institutions, Behavior, Public Sphere and Diversity (INCT ID-ICED), as well as GEMAA, the Brazilian Legislative Observatory (OLB), and the Laboratory for Media and Public Sphere Studies (LEMEP), which hosts the Manchetômetro project.
